diagnosis.signal: PayFlux's pricing page receives 8,200 unique monthly visitors with an average session duration of 6.3 minutes — indicating genuine purchase intent. Yet the free-to-paid conversion rate sits at 4.1%. The revenue gap between intent and action is $38,000/month at current traffic levels.

friction.rootCause: The pricing grid exposes 5 plans with 22 feature line-items each. Users must become product experts before selecting a plan. The cognitive overhead of self-classifying into the correct tier exceeds the motivation threshold for 96% of visitors.

decisions.label: Collapse to 3 plans with 5 features each
decisions.action: Reduce visible plans from 5 to 3 (Starter, Growth, Enterprise). Show only 5 key differentiating features per plan. Gate full feature comparison behind a 'See all features' expand toggle.
decisions.reasoning: Hick's Law: decision time increases logarithmically with options. Cutting from 5 to 3 plans and 22 to 5 features reduces the decision load by 73%. Baymard research shows this pattern increases checkout initiation by 35-50% in SaaS contexts.
decisions.tradeoff: Requires rewriting the pricing page copy and design. Some power users may want the full feature list — satisfy them with the progressive disclosure toggle.

decisions.label: Replace pricing grid with a usage-based calculator
decisions.action: Eliminate the tier grid entirely. Replace with a single interactive calculator: 'How many payment transactions per month?' → outputs one number: your monthly cost. Show the ROI delta versus Stripe's 2.9% + 30¢ standard rate.
decisions.reasoning: Removes 100% of the self-classification burden. Users never need to guess which plan fits them — the system calculates it instantly. This is especially powerful for a payments product where the value proposition is directly tied to volume.
decisions.tradeoff: Requires engineering for the calculator. Pricing model must be directly translatable to a usage formula. If enterprise contracts have custom pricing, gate those above a volume threshold.

decisions.label: Lead with ROI, bury the price
decisions.action: Restructure the page: show the savings calculator first, the plan selector second. Default the calculator to 10,000 transactions/month (your average ICP). Show the monthly savings vs. current payment stack before revealing the subscription cost.
decisions.reasoning: Anchors value before cost. When users see '$2,400 in annual savings' before seeing '$79/month', the price becomes a no-brainer. This ordering shift alone has produced 60%+ conversion rate increases in analogous fintech contexts.
decisions.tradeoff: Requires a full page restructure. Copy must be rewritten around the savings narrative rather than the feature narrative.
